text: {"domains":{"block_M":[32,64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3],"threads":[128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.5,"launches":1,"pipeline":2,"footprint":1},"rationale":"Four attempts observed. baseline (128,64,64,st=1,sw=0): 2558.09 us, 531.63 MB. Then sw=16 variants: (64,128,64,st=1,sw=16) 1616.24 us / 269.75 MB; (64,128,32,st=2,sw=16) 1597.23 us / 269.68 MB (current best); (64,128,32,st=1,sw=16) 1912.58 us / 269.68 MB. Key facts: serpentine swizzle gave the large step (~40% latency, ~half DRAM); after swizzle, DRAM is saturated at ~269.7 MB and further tile/stage changes only shift latency modestly, while stages=2 beat stages=1 at same tile (1597 vs 1913 us) implying pipelining matters and stages=1 is poor when swizzle holds traffic fixed. Also 1912.58 us at same DRAM as 1597.23 us shows traffic weight alone cannot rank configs—traffic saturated, so pipeline term is the discriminative signal. Thus raise pipeline weight to 2 (reward deeper stages) while keeping traffic=1.5 to still prefer swizzle>0 and larger panels, launches=1, footprint=1. Keep shared_memory_limit at the 32768-byte portability cap; all observed compiled smem was exactly 32768 B, so no headroom evidence to raise, and cap is also the portability ceiling. Keep full tile/stage/swizzle domains since everything divides 4096 and exclusions have not made any subset infeasible; swizzle=[0,4,8,16] retained per feedback rules though sw=0 is demonstrably worse at baseline. Prior four tuples are excluded, so HiGHS must pick a new point. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with swizzle in {8,16} and stages≥2 should further reduce simulated latency via larger serpentine panels plus pipelining; if DRAM stays ~270 MB and latency does not improve with stages=3 or block_M=128, traffic/pipeline weights are mis-set and should move toward footprint/launches. Proxy is dimensionless ranking only, not microseconds. Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR but CUDA binaries are not executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed."}
